messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test `testOverrideVarianceWithMathClass` sets a custom Variance implementation (with population variance) to the SummaryStatistics instance by calling `setVarianceImpl(new Variance(false))`. After adding values to the SummaryStatistics, the test asserts that the variance computed by the SummaryStatistics matches that computed directly by the Variance instance on the same dataset.

The current bug report describes that after setting the variance implementation with `setVarianceImpl(new Variance(true/false))`, calling `getStandardDeviation()` produces NaN.

Looking at `SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic varianceImpl)`, this method sets the internal varianceImpl to the provided implementation, but first calls `checkEmpty()` which likely validates that no data has been added yet.

`SummaryStatistics.getStandardDeviation()` returns NaN by default but returns the square root of `getVariance()` if there is more than one data point.

`SummaryStatistics.getVariance()` delegates to `varianceImpl.getResult()` to get the current variance.

`SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)` increments various statistics. Notably, if the varianceImpl is not an instance of `Variance`, it increments it with the value. But if it is an instance of Variance (like when the varianceImpl was overridden), it does NOT call `varianceImpl.increment(value)`.

This is key to the problem: when we replace the varianceImpl with a new Variance instance by `setVarianceImpl(new Variance(false))`, the varianceImpl is an instance of Variance, so the check in addValue:

```
if (!(varianceImpl instanceof Variance)) {
    varianceImpl.increment(value);
}
```

is false, so `varianceImpl.increment(value)` is NOT called for the new Variance instance.

Therefore, even after adding values via SummaryStatistics.addValue, the overridden varianceImpl Variance has no updated data and its `getResult()` returns NaN, leading `getVariance()` and `getStandardDeviation()` to return NaN.

In contrast, if the varianceImpl was a different implementation than Variance, it would get correctly incremented by these addValue calls.

This explains the test failure: the varianceImpl is replaced with a Variance instance, but that instance does not get incremented by addValue, so its state is empty and `getResult()` returns NaN.

In summary, the bug is in `SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)`. When the varianceImpl is an instance of Variance, addValue does not update it with new values, causing getVariance/getStandardDeviation to return NaN after setVarianceImpl with Variance.

No recent bug reports seem related to this specific problem.

# Final Diagnosis:
Replacing varianceImpl with a Variance instance causes addValue to skip incrementing it, leaving varianceImpl empty and leading to getStandardDeviation producing NaN. This is due to the check in addValue that only increments the varianceImpl if it is NOT an instance of Variance.

The failing test `testOverrideVarianceWithMathClass` reveals this issue because it overrides varianceImpl with `new Variance(false)` and expects consistent results, but gets NaN from getStandardDeviation instead.

This indicates addValue should be adjusted to always increment varianceImpl regardless of type or handle the case when the varianceImpl is replaced with a fresh Variance instance.

---

Next, I will specify the methods which should be fixed based on this analysis.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
